standard_prerequisites.name: Recurring matrices and the max-modulus argument
standard_prerequisites.statement: A real matrix A with nonnegative off-diagonal entries together with a positive vector m such that minus a of subscript i i times m of subscript i is at least the sum of a of subscript i j times m of subscript j over the other indices is what the chapter calls a recurring matrix for m; the classical diagonal-dominance argument of Taussky, quoted by the author in the neighbouring lemma lemma-recurring of this same chapter, gives the nonsingularity statement that the present lemma refines. The author's own definitions are retained in the span of the counted lemma.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the structural refinement of the diagonal-dominance criterion for recurring matrices, and its proof is the same maximal-coordinate argument carried through with equality analysis.

core_obligations: Reduce to the case of the all-ones vector: replace each entry a of subscript i j by a of subscript i j times m of subscript j, which leaves the hypothesis and the conclusion unchanged, so that m may be taken to be the all-ones vector (source line 352).

One inclusion: for a subset I satisfying the two displayed conditions, verify by a direct computation that the vector supported on I with coordinates m of subscript i is in the kernel of A (source lines 353-354).

The other inclusion by induction on the number of nonzero coordinates of a kernel vector x: let I be the set of indices where the absolute value of the coordinate of x is maximal and show that the chain of inequalities bounding a of subscript r r times x of subscript r from below is an equality chain, so that a of subscript r k vanishes for r in I and k outside I and equality holds in the displayed inequality for r in I (source lines 355-368).

Finish the induction step: the vector x sub I just exhibited satisfies the two conditions, so subtracting a suitable multiple of it from x decreases the number of nonzero coordinates and the induction hypothesis applies (source lines 367-370).

proof_roadmap.step: Rescale the entries by the vector m so that m is the all-ones vector.
Show that every vector supported on a set satisfying the two conditions lies in the kernel.
Maximal-coordinate argument: the inequality chain for an index of maximal absolute value is an equality chain, forcing the vanishing conditions.
Subtract a multiple of the exhibited kernel vector to decrease the number of nonzero coordinates and conclude by induction.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 Stacks Project 章 models.tex 的 Lemma lemma-recurring-real（源 330-349 行，证明 351-370 行）：给定非对角元非负的实矩阵 A 与正向量 m，若对每个 i 都有 −a_ii m_i ≥ Σ_{j≠i} a_ij m_j，则 Ker(A) 恰由「在满足两条条件（I 与补集之间无非零耦合；等式在 I 上成立）的指标集上支集的向量」张成。关键操作不是例行核验：先把 m 归一化（352 行），再证一个方向（353-354 行），最后用「取 |x_r| 最大的指标集 I」把不等式链逼成等式链，从而同时得到 a_{rk}=0（r∈I, k∉I）与等式成立两条结构结论（355-366 行），再减去合适的 x_I 倍数把非零坐标数严格下降、对非零坐标个数归纳（367-370 行）。难点在于必须从「不等式链上每一处都取等」同时导出零模式与等号模式这两条结构信息，而不是只得到核的包含关系；原文位置在证明的 352、353-354、355-366、367-370 行。
